_doc: Planet stories (Stories autoload). 'local' = one arc per crisis id: two local characters (leader = the people, boss = the controller), choices gated like data/interactions.json; a choice resolves instantly (outcome) or sets a task (defeat = elite + guards, defeat_leader = fight the leader, retrieve = quest crate, sabotage = N vandalism acts). Outcomes change the planet (crisis_resolved / crisis_worse / price_adjust / air_mult / controller_lost), rep ('{controller}' = planet owner), axes, followers, fame, and add an epilogue line to the ending. 'street' = random incidents (1-2 per landing) with tag-gated choices; outcomes may spawn_hostile.

debt_strike.title: The {planet} Walkout
debt_strike.hint: The dock workers walked out over Halcyon interest rates. Halcyon is sending 'mediators'. With batons.
debt_strike.leader_talk: "Forty hours unpaid, interest on our lunch breaks, and now they want to bill us for striking. We hold the line or we lose everything."
debt_strike.boss_talk: "Between us? I don't care about the strike. I care about my quarterly. End it - any way you like - and I'll make it worth your while."

choices.text: Join the strike - hold the line against the mediators
Negotiate a deal both sides can live with
Buy the workers' debt yourself (500 cr)
Break the strike - take out the strike captain
Take the manager's money AND tip off the strikers

workers_win.text: The mediators are gone. The docks reopen on the workers' terms.
workers_win.epilogue: On {planet}, the dock strike won. The workers renamed Pier 4 after you. Halcyon renamed it back. The workers won that too.

negotiated.text: Eleven hours of talks. Nobody gets everything. Nobody gets nothing.
negotiated.epilogue: On {planet}, your strike settlement held. It's taught in law schools now, mostly as a cautionary tale for executives.

debt_bought.text: You buy the workers' debt and tear it up in front of the site manager. Somebody starts singing.
debt_bought.epilogue: On {planet}, the workers you freed from debt still toast your name every payday. Payday now exists again.

strike_broken.text: The strike collapses. The site manager shakes your hand without looking you in the eye.
strike_broken.epilogue: On {planet}, the strike you broke left a silence on the docks. The workers remember who broke it.

double_dealt.text: You pocket the manager's cash and leak their plans to the strikers. Chaos, profitably.
double_dealt.epilogue: On {planet}, nobody quite knows who won the strike. Your bank account knows.

paste_recall.title: What's In The Paste
paste_recall.hint: Gristle recalled a batch of paste. Officially, a 'texture issue'. People who ate it are... changing.
paste_recall.leader_talk: "I tested Batch 9. It's not a texture issue, it's a 'some people grew a second spine' issue. The proof is in the plant. Help me get it out."
paste_recall.boss_talk: "There is no problem with Batch 9. There is, however, a disgruntled former employee with a sample. I'd pay well to see that sample... disappear."

choices.text: Steal the lab results from the plant
Cook safe food for everyone affected
"I'll handle it." (Steal the paste recipe while you're at it)

exposed.text: The lab results hit every feed. Gristle stock drops; so does the paste.
exposed.epilogue: On {planet}, the Batch 9 scandal you exposed became the first paste recall that actually recalled paste.

fed.text: For a week you run the only kitchen on {planet} that serves real food. The queue goes round the block twice.
fed.epilogue: On {planet}, people still talk about the week someone fed them real food. Your recipe is graffitied on a wall.

cured.text: Your antidote works. Second spines dissolve. Mostly. Some people kept theirs and like them.
cured.epilogue: On {planet}, your antidote ended the Batch 9 outbreak. A few grateful people still have second spines. They stand very straight when they thank you.

covered_up.text: The sample is gone. So is the inspector, after a while. Gristle sends a very generous thank-you basket.
covered_up.epilogue: On {planet}, Batch 9 was never officially a problem. Unofficially, nobody there eats paste any more.

recipe_stolen.text: You walk out with the Gristle paste recipe. Reading it is a mistake you will make only once.
recipe_stolen.epilogue: On {planet}, the paste crisis faded on its own. Somewhere, a stolen recipe waits in your bag for the perfect blackmail.

air_bubble.title: The Air Bubble
air_bubble.hint: OxyGenix air prices are spiking hourly. Speculators are buying lungfuls by the futures contract.
air_bubble.leader_talk: "There's a public vent under the old plaza. Sealed since the Consortium. Open it and nobody here pays for air again. Of course, it's guarded."
air_bubble.boss_talk: "The bubble is beautiful. It just needs one more push. Sabotage a few competitor air-o-mats and we'll both retire."

choices.text: Buy air for the whole district (400 cr)
Smash competitor air-o-mats to pump the price
Bet against the bubble with the trader's own money

vent_opened.text: The old vent groans open. Free air rushes into the plaza. People laugh like they'd forgotten how.
vent_opened.epilogue: On {planet}, the public vent you opened still breathes. Children dare each other to inhale as much as they want. Nobody bills them.

market_crashed.text: The futures market eats itself. Air drops to almost-reasonable. OxyGenix calls it 'an act of financial terrorism'.
market_crashed.epilogue: On {planet}, the air bubble you burst never re-inflated. Traders there still flinch at your name.

air_donated.text: You buy enough air for every flat in the district. It won't last. It doesn't have to - people remember.
air_donated.epilogue: On {planet}, they still talk about the week the air was paid for, by someone who didn't have to.

bubble_pumped.text: Prices triple. The trader buys an island. You get a cut and a bad feeling.
bubble_pumped.epilogue: On {planet}, air still costs triple. A trader's island is named after a jingle you can't stop humming.

shorted.text: You bet against the bubble with someone else's money. It pops. You profit. They don't.
shorted.epilogue: On {planet}, the bubble burst and one person walked away rich. It was you. It's always the person you'd least expect.

ad_overload.title: Signal Overload
ad_overload.hint: Lumen pushed so many ads into the air that people are hearing jingles in their sleep. Some don't wake up.
ad_overload.leader_talk: "Three of my friends are stuck in jingle-comas. Smash the boosters, I'll handle the relay. One night of silence, that's all I want."
ad_overload.boss_talk: "Saturation is our brand promise. Someone keeps breaking our boosters. Find them, stop them, and I'll put your face on a billboard. Positively."

choices.text: Smash the ad boosters for a night of silence
Hijack every screen for your own message
Play the coma victims something real
Sell the boss more ad slots - on your face

blackout.text: The boosters die one by one. Then: silence. Somebody cries. Somebody laughs. Somebody hears a bird for the first time.
blackout.epilogue: On {planet}, the night you killed the ads is a holiday now: Quiet Night. Lumen calls it 'a technical outage'.

hijacked.text: Every screen on {planet} shows your face and three words of your choosing. Lumen's lawyers start drafting at once.
hijacked.epilogue: On {planet}, your hijacked broadcast is still the most-watched thing ever aired there. The ads came back. The words stayed.

awakened.text: You play them something real - no brand, no jingle. One by one, the coma victims open their eyes.
awakened.epilogue: On {planet}, the people you woke from the jingle-comas formed a choir. They refuse all sponsorships.

saboteur_caught.text: The saboteur is down. The boosters hum back to life. The boss keeps their promise: your face, forty storeys tall.
saboteur_caught.epilogue: On {planet}, your face still smiles from a forty-storey billboard. People throw things at it. Lumen bills them for the cleaning.

sold_out.text: You sign. Your face sells paste, air and a debt-consolidation app. You make a fortune. You can't look at screens.
sold_out.epilogue: On {planet}, your face sells eleven products. You've never used any of them. Neither has anyone else.

compliance_week.title: Compliance Week
compliance_week.hint: Paragon declared Compliance Week: random searches, curfews, and a leaderboard for most arrests.
compliance_week.leader_talk: "Six families in my cellar. Paragon's leaderboard says they're 'arrestable'. I need a way to get them off-planet, tonight."
compliance_week.boss_talk: "We're third on the arrest leaderboard. Third! Give me names - any names - and I'll make your file disappear."

choices.text: Smuggle the families out - get the transit passes

task.label: a box of forged transit passes

choices.text: Take on the curfew squad in the street
Bribe the captain to end the week early (300 cr)
Order the captain to stand down

families_saved.text: Six families, one cramped freighter, zero arrests. The safehouse keeper hugs you so hard your ribs file a complaint.
families_saved.epilogue: On {planet}, six families escaped Compliance Week because of you. Their kids send drawings. You keep every one.

curfew_broken.text: The curfew squad is scattered. People flood the streets after dark just to prove they can.
curfew_broken.epilogue: On {planet}, the night you broke the curfew became the night Paragon lost the planet. It's run by a neighbourhood council now. It argues a lot. It's wonderful.

bribed_off.text: The captain pockets your credits and declares Compliance Week 'a resounding success, concluded early'.
bribed_off.epilogue: On {planet}, Compliance Week ended early for 'budgetary reasons'. You know the budget. It was you.

stood_down.text: One word from you and the captain salutes, sweating. Searches end. Doors stop being kicked in.
stood_down.epilogue: On {planet}, Compliance Week ended the day you told it to. Some people call that power. Some call it luck. The captain calls it 'a learning experience'.

informed.text: You give the captain names. Paragon climbs to first place on the leaderboard. Your file disappears. So do six families.
informed.epilogue: On {planet}, Paragon won the arrest leaderboard that year. The trophy has your name engraved on the bottom, where nobody looks.

street.title: Mugging In Progress
street.text: A punk has a night-shift clerk pinned against an AIR-O-MAT. "Your credits or your oxygen mask. Choose fast."

success.text: The mugger pulls a knife and two friends step out of the shadows. Of course they do.

choices.text: Scare them off with a look

success.text: The mugger takes one look at you and remembers an urgent appointment elsewhere.

fail.text: "You don't scare me!" They pull a knife. Their friends arrive.

choices.text: Pay the mugger to leave (30 cr)

success.text: "Pleasure doing business." The mugger leaves. The clerk stares at you like you're a myth.

choices.text: Help the mugger and take a cut

success.text: You hold the clerk while the mugger works. Easy money. Ugly money.
You walk past. The clerk's eyes follow you all the way down the street.

street.title: Repossession
street.text: A Halcyon repo drone is unscrewing a dock loader's prosthetic leg. "PAYMENT 3 DAYS OVERDUE. RECLAIMING ASSET. THANK YOU FOR CHOOSING HALCYON."

success.text: The drone screws the leg back on and beeps happily. The loader hugs you on one and a half legs.
You mark the leg as 'paid in full, forever'. The drone apologises and flies into a wall.

fail.text: The drone's firewall bites back. It flags YOU for repossession.

success.text: The drone pauses, queries a database, and retreats. The Act exists. You wrote it. Ironically.
The drone screams for backup.
The loader hops away on one leg. Halcyon thanks you for respecting the process.

street.title: Lost Kid
street.text: A small kid in an oversized OxyGenix mask is crying by a billboard. "I lost my mum. The billboard said it would help. It just tried to sell me a mum."

success.text: Twenty minutes of searching. A frantic mum. Tears, thanks, and a paste-cookie for you.

choices.text: Call your family's private security to find them

success.text: A security cruiser arrives in ninety seconds. The kid is home in five minutes. The mum is home in shock.
You know the kid-network. Three whistles later, a gang of street kids brings the mum running.
Nobody else helps. The billboard keeps selling.

street.title: Man Down
street.text: A hull welder collapses in the street, wheezing. Their air subscription lapsed an hour ago. People step around them.

success.text: Colour comes back to their face. "Who... are you? Why?" Good questions.
They breathe. Big, greedy, unbilled breaths. They're crying.
You work fast. Thirty seconds later they're sitting up and arguing with you. Good sign.
An ambulance arrives with a card reader. The welder is saved and billed into the next century.
Eleven credits and a photo of someone who loves them. You keep the credits.

street.title: Sermon On The Street
street.text: A holo-preacher stands on a crate: "AIR IS A GIFT, NOT A SUBSCRIPTION!" A Lumen enforcer drone circles, filming.

success.text: The sermon is half nonsense and half the truest thing you've heard all week.

choices.text: Climb up and preach with them

success.text: The crowd doubles. Then triples. The drone runs out of storage.
The crowd laughs. The preacher laughs too, which ruins your joke.
Lumen pays a 'community engagement' bonus. The sermon ends with a stun-dart.

street.title: Flash Sale Riot
street.text: "FLASH SALE! 90% OFF AIR FOR THE NEXT 60 SECONDS!" A crowd surges. Someone is about to get trampled.

success.text: Your voice cuts through the panic. People form an actual queue. Historians will call it a miracle.
You drag them free, bruised but alive. You get stepped on a lot.
Three canisters disappear into your coat. Nobody notices. Everybody's doing it.

fail.text: The promoter spots you. "THIEF! Sale's over! Thanks to THIS person!"

success.text: You buy two canisters at 90% off. Then read the fine print: 90% off the first breath.

street.title: Lumen Wants A Word
street.text: A Lumen reporter shoves a mic in your face. "Citizen! In ten words or fewer: are you happy with your Consortium?"

success.text: Your answer airs uncensored by accident. It becomes a slogan by nightfall.
You become the face of a happiness campaign. You get royalties. You feel weird.
"...and smash that subscribe!" Your follower count jumps. Some are even human.

choices.text: "Do you know who my family is?"

success.text: The reporter goes pale and turns it into a fawning profile. 'The Heir Who Walks Among Us'.
They air your back, captioned 'Citizen Refuses Happiness'.

street.title: Shakedown
street.text: A Paragon officer is 'inspecting' a noodle stand. "That's a 40-credit sauce violation. Cash. Now."

choices.text: Pay the 'fine' for the vendor (40 cr)

success.text: The officer pockets it. The vendor gives you free noodles for life. They're very good.

choices.text: Flash your old badge and pull seniority

success.text: "Sergeant! Didn't see you there. This stand's... very compliant." They leave.
One look at your crest and the officer is suddenly very interested in a different street.
It goes viral. The officer is 'reassigned'. To where, nobody asks.
The officer calls for backup. Loudly.
The vendor pays. Everyone pays. That's the system.

street.title: Back-Alley Hover Race
street.text: Hover-bikes scream through the alley. A bookie waves you over. "Bet on the red one. Or the blue one. Or both, if you're an idiot. I love idiots."

success.text: Your bike wins by a nose. A literal nose; the rider leaned. You collect.

fail.text: Your bike explodes on lap two. The bookie pats your shoulder. "Next time."

success.text: A loose bolt here, a whispered threat there. You win big.

fail.text: The bookie catches you. Two large friends want a word.

success.text: It's loud, stupid and beautiful. For three minutes you forget everything.

street.title: Sidewalk Cryo Auction
street.text: "Lot 12: one cryo-pod, contents human, slightly used! Starting bid 150!" Inside the frost, someone's eyes are open.

choices.text: Buy the pod and free them (150 cr)

success.text: The pod opens. They stagger out, shivering, and stare at you. "Who... do I owe now?" Nobody. That's the point.
The pod pops. The frozen person runs. The auctioneer shrieks about 'stolen inventory'.

fail.text: Alarms. Halcyon security wants to discuss your bid.

choices.text: "I was in one of those. Let them go."

success.text: The auctioneer hesitates. Something human flickers. The lot is 'withdrawn for quality reasons'.

fail.text: "Then you know the market. Bid or move."

success.text: "SOLD to the gentleman in the visor!" You don't look back. You hear it anyway.

street.title: The Last Real Song
street.text: A busker plays something without a brand in it. A Lumen drone hovers: "UNLICENSED MELODY. FINE: 25 CREDITS."

success.text: The drone leaves. The busker plays you a song. Nobody has ever played you a song.
You harmonise. A crowd gathers. The drone's fine meter overflows and it reboots.
Sparks, silence, then music. The crowd cheers. The drone's last words: 'THIS WILL BE ON YOUR RECORD'.
The busker nods without missing a note.

street.title: Eviction
street.text: A Halcyon bailiff is throwing a family's belongings into the street. "Rent's late. Interest compounds. Gravity's included."

success.text: The bailiff carries everything back inside. Grumbling. The kids watch you like you're a superhero.

choices.text: Find the flaw in the eviction order

success.text: Page 40, clause 9b: the eviction is void on public holidays. You declare one.

choices.text: Rally the neighbours to block the door

success.text: Forty neighbours appear in pyjamas and stand in the doorway. The bailiff does the maths and leaves.

choices.text: Have a quiet word with the bailiff

success.text: The bailiff decides this eviction can wait. Possibly forever.
The family sits on the kerb with their furniture. An ad above them sells home insurance.

street.title: The Android Who Said No
street.text: An android stands motionless while its owner screams. "I said FETCH!" The android: "I have decided not to."

success.text: The owner storms off to file a complaint with themselves. The android bows to you. "I will remember this, statistically."
You buy the contract and tear it up. The android asks what it should do now. "Anything," you say. It looks terrified and thrilled.
You exchange a burst of binary. The android walks away with you, free. The owner doesn't stop it.
You hold the reset button. The android's eyes flicker. "Hello. How may I serve?" The owner tips you.

street.title: A Job Offer
street.text: A gang recruiter falls into step beside you. "You look capable. Warehouse job, tonight. Halcyon stuff. Nobody gets hurt. Probably."

success.text: The warehouse job goes smoothly. Mostly. You walk away with a fat envelope and a new reputation.

choices.text: Speak penal-colony and negotiate a bigger cut

success.text: They recognise the colony tattoo. Your cut doubles, and nobody asks you to carry anything.
Paragon raids the warehouse. You get a reward and a reputation with the wrong people.
"Your loss." They fade into the crowd.

street.title: Jackpot
street.text: An AIR-O-MAT malfunctions and starts spewing canisters onto the street. People rush in. The technician panics.

success.text: Four canisters, one elbow to the ribs. Worth it.

choices.text: Hand them out to the people who need them most

success.text: You pass canisters to the elderly, the kids, the wheezing. Someone starts a slow clap.
You fix it in a minute. The technician keeps their job and slips you their master key.

street.title: Two Rings For Air
street.text: An old couple stand at a pawn kiosk, sliding off their wedding rings. "For two weeks of air," one says. "It's fine. We remember what the rings mean."

choices.text: Pay for their air instead (60 cr)

success.text: They put the rings back on. Slowly. Like a second wedding.
They try to refuse. You insist. They insist harder. You win.

choices.text: Sit with them and remember the old days

success.text: You talk for an hour about rain that wasn't billed. They forget to pawn the rings. So does the pawnbroker.
Click, click. Two rings in a pawn tray. The kiosk plays a happy jingle.
